items.title: Iranian forces on higher alert, stronger than before war, spokesman says
items.summary: Iranian forces on higher alert, stronger than before war, spokesman says Iran's military is "stronger" and more motivated than it was when the United States and Israel started the war in February, says Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia. "Today, the Islamic Republic's armed forces... having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war," Akraminia said, according to the state news agency Irna. "They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence." Akraminia said that Iranian armed forces retained control over the Strait of Hormuz and that it would remain closed until the United States accepted Tehran's demands. "Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations," he added.

items.summary: According to President Donald Trump, he and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu have agreed to end the “$4 billion a year” in U.S. aid to Israel by the end of 2026. This is the first anyone has heard about this, at least publicly. It will be interesting to see how Netanyahu reacts to Trump’s seemingly impromptu announcement on FOX News’ “Fox & Friends” morning talk show Tuesday morning. The embattled Israeli leader is on the record saying he wanted another Memorandum of Understanding allocating the annual funds until tapering off at the end of “10 years.” He is also embroiled in a live leadership fight in which he may or may not lose his prime ministership. The annual $3.8 aid package does not expire until 2028. What is Trump up to here? On one hand, he may be desperately trying to signal to Republican voters on election day that his party is not slavishly beholden to Israel, as a growing clique on his right flank now alleges. items.title: Voormalig Midden-Oostencorrespondent Thomas Loudon (56) overleden
items.summary: Journalist en oud-correspondent Thomas Loudon is overleden. Hij kampte met neuro-endocriene tumoren (NET), een langzaam groeiende vorm van kanker. Vorig jaar kreeg hij de diagnose en deze week overleed hij daaraan. Hij was 56 jaar. In 2001 werd Loudon de eerste Nederlandse (video)journalist die zich na de Islamitische Revolutie in Iran vestigde. Hij deed in diverse talen verslag van ontwikkelingen in Iran, Afghanistan en het noorden van Irak voor onder meer de NOS, Trouw en Elsevier, maar ook voor buitenlandse media als CNN, het Chileense Canal 13 en Asia TV in Singapore. Egypte en Jordanië In 2003 trok hij naar de Egyptische hoofdstad Caïro, waar hij Midden-Oostencorrespondent werd voor de NOS. Daarna deed hij dat vanuit Jordanië. Hij maakte onder meer verhalen over de Amerikaanse oorlog in Irak. Correspondent bleef hij tot begin 2007, waarna hij terugkeerde naar Nederland. In de jaren daarna was hij actief als docent journalistiek in Groningen en Rotterdam. items.title: Europeans got blue blinders in wake of midterm sweep
items.summary: The Democratic sweep of the midterm elections has been greeted with a wary relief across Europe. After two years of President Donald Trump's tariffs, threats to annex Greenland and scolding of European NATO allies on defense spending, many European politicians see the Republican defeat as a welcome course correction. Yet the reactions also expose the contradictions of the European Union’s own foreign policy, particularly toward the wars in Iran and Ukraine. Rather than examining the causes of Trump’s defeat, EU leaders have chosen to interpret it as a vindication of their own ideological beliefs. The EU high representative for foreign policy, Kaja Kallas, unsurprisingly, saw in the election a hope that the new Congress will strengthen transatlantic unity and support for Ukraine, presumably reversing Trump’s insufficient devotion to the Ukrainian cause, which she criticized earlier. Europe has to show the saboteurs that we are resilient It was as though a ghostly hand had switched the settings on supermarket freezers across Europe from “freeze” to “defrost”. From Finland to Ireland, they suddenly began heating up , many reaching 50C and food worth millions of euros had to be thrown away. But no actual hand was needed to cause the meltdown. This was a cyber-attack, or rather a chain of attacks. Like pretty much everything else in 2026, supermarket freezers are digitally enabled. That makes them smarter and more efficient, but like everything else that is connected to the internet, it also makes them more vulnerable. Russian hacktivists claimed they were behind some of the supermarket sabotage, but no one knows for sure. It could also be Iran, Iranian proxies, North Korea – or unaffiliated bedroom hackers. When Transport for London suffered a devastating hack two years ago, the culprits turned out to be two British teenagers . items.summary: Trump admits Iran war caused election losses but ‘we had to do it’ US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that the Iran war was responsible for his Republican Party's resounding midterm election defeat. Asked whether he agreed with Vice President JD Vance earlier remarks that the Iran war was "the reason we lost", Trump told reporters outside the White House ballroom construction site that his comments were "largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit short term". "But at the same time, if I had it to do again, I'd have to do it again. Because long term, it's the only answer. You can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon," he added. He also ruled out firing Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, saying "he's doing a very good job," despite his role in pushing for military action against Tehran. items.title: Major losses could spur Trump to escalate war before year's end
items.summary: As much as the Iran war is the key reason Trump and the GOP were crushed tonight, it is important to recognize that the pressure for war is now likely to increase . This does not mean that Trump will restart the war. But the balance of pressure for and against war will likely favor escalation. Trump was under a degree of pressure to strike a deal before the midterms, hoping to soften the blow in the polls. But now that the midterms are over, that pressure will dissipate somewhat. Gas prices are still high, but the political cost has already been paid. There won’t be another point on the political calendar for some time when that cost can be exacted again. But two other factors will intensify. First, pro-war elements in Israel and in Washington will see the next two months as the last period in which Trump has wide maneuverability to restart the war. By January, the Democrats will control both chambers, will control the purse, and can begin impeaching Trump’s secretaries, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. items.summary: US and Iran edge closer to potential breakthrough in talks to end war, Bloomberg reports The United States and Iran are moving closer to a possible breakthrough in efforts to end the war, with Tehran considering proposals on its nuclear programme that it had previously been unwilling to discuss, Bloomberg reported, citing a diplomat familiar with the talks. The diplomat said Iran was studying proposals on its nuclear activities presented by Qatar, the main mediator. Any concession could help to advance negotiations, which have stalled since the collapse of an interim agreement reached in June. Reuters and The New York Times have also previously reported on Iran’s willingness to compromise on the nuclear issue. US President Donald Trump spoke by phone with Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani about efforts to de-escalate the conflict and secure a comprehensive agreement, the emir’s office said on Friday. Qatari officials have been shuttling between Doha and Tehran to help bridge differences, including over Iran’s nuclear activities and the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

items.title: Aipac spent $55m on losing congressional candidates in midterm elections: Report
items.summary: Aipac spent $55m on losing congressional candidates in midterm elections: Report The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (Aipac) spent more than $84m in the 2026 US midterms, but nearly two-thirds of those funds were spent on losing candidates, according to a new report from Responsible Statecraft. Aipac’s Super Pac and other groups spent $55m on failed candidates. The largest portion of those funds, about $32m, was spent trying to defeat Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan. The results marked one of Aipac’s worst performances in years, suggesting that the US-Israeli war on Iran, which has contributed to soaring cost-of-living issues, resonated strongly with voters. In the 2022 midterms, Aipac’s Super Pac, United Democracy Project, saw 69 percent of its expenditure spent on races backed by the organisation that won. That number was even higher in 2024, after Israel’s genocide in Gaza, with 87 percent of its spending going to successful races. The group was an early supporter of the war and a major funder of ads attacking House and Senate candidates calling to cut off aid to Israel. It spent big on the 2026 midterm elections, dumping $84.1 million via its super PAC, United Democracy Project (UDP), and several other PACs into races that have been decided as of this writing. Iranian negotiators held talks with Qatari mediators in Doha to discuss paths out of the war, Reuters reported earlier on Saturday, citing a source who spoke on condition of anonymity. Saturday’s talks in the Qatari capital followed more than 12 hours of discussions on Friday between Iranian and Qatari envoys in Tehran, the source said.

items.title: What the Midterms Mean for U.S. Foreign Policy
items.summary: If the polls are right, Democrats will retake at least one chamber of Congress in the U.S. midterms. And with voters focused on the cost of living, foreign policy is an unusually impactful driver at the ballot box: Tariffs have raised the price of everyday goods, and the war with Iran has sent gas prices soaring. How might Democrats use their new power over spending and oversight to challenge Trump’s agenda in his final two years in office? How will allies and adversaries read the results? Susan Glasser, a staff writer at the New Yorker and former editor in chief of Foreign Policy, will join FP Live to break down what the midterms mean for congressional power and for America’s standing in the world.

items.summary: Trump says US knocked out Iranian 'little bit of anti-aircraft device' US President Donald Trump says Washington had made considerable progress in its dealings with Iran, while acknowledging that US forces had carried out limited strikes against targets on the country. "I don't want to talk about it. We do minor strikes. But they knocked out... and they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device. And we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five," Trump told reporters when asked about reports of strikes near Iran's Qeshm Island. Speaking to reporters after arriving aboard Air Force One at Donald J. Trump International Airport, Trump said the United States was taking out more Iranian oil than before the conflict. "We've made a lot of progress with Iran, we're taking out more oil now than we were before the war. It's not a war," he said. "You know, in Russia-Ukraine, they lose 25,000 people a month. items.summary: UKMTO says 11 ships attacked in week to 4 Nov in Hormuz, Arabian Gulf The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) has reported 11 attacks on commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and Arabian Gulf in the seven days to November 4, including incidents that left three vessels sunk. Eight attacks occurred in the Strait of Hormuz and three in the Arabian Gulf, according to UKMTO's weekly overview. Of the 11 incidents, three vessels continued their voyages, five required assistance and three sank. The report said one dhow was struck by an unidentified projectile on 2 November, killing one crew member, while 13 others were rescued by local authorities. A Panama-flagged supply vessel was also struck by an unidentified projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on 1 November and reportedly sank after a nearby merchant vessel rescued its crew. A Marshall Islands-flagged tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles in the Arabian Gulf on 4 November, leaving it drifting and requiring assistance from local authorities. items.summary: Iran's health ministry denies report on iodine distribution over US strike fears Iran's health ministry has denied a report by The Times of London that it was distributing iodine tablets near its nuclear sites to prepare for possible US strikes. "No Ministry of Health official has spoken to The Times, and the quote attributed to the ministry is false," Hossein Kermanpour, head of the ministry's public relations and information centre, wrote on X . He said the health system was prepared for various scenarios and threats from "an enemy that does not even spare children". But he added that declaring a state of war was not within the ministry's authority. He called publishing unverified reports at such a time "irresponsible". The Times of London had cited an unnamed health ministry official who said Iran was handing out iodine tablets to communities near its nuclear facilities. The official was quoted as saying, “Trump can no longer be trusted. clusters.headline: US issues new Iran sanctions as Trump says talks with Tehran going 'very well'

items.title: US issues new Iran sanctions as Trump says talks with Tehran going 'very well'
items.summary: US issues new Iran sanctions as Trump says talks with Tehran going 'very well' US President Donald Trump said on Friday that his administration was in talks with Iranian representatives, telling reporters: "We are doing very well with Iran." His comments came as the US Treasury Department imposed new Iran-related sanctions on eight entities based in Canada, according to a notice on its website. In a separate move on Friday, the Treasury blocked US banks from dealing with MEXC Global, a cryptocurrency exchange registered in the Seychelles. It accused the exchange of handling at least $16bn in illegal transactions linked to Iran, North Korea and Russia, helping them get around sanctions. On Thursday, the Treasury sanctioned companies and individuals in India and Turkey that it accused of helping Iran evade restrictions on its oil exports and airlines. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the same day that Washington would continue to pursue anyone supporting Tehran. Referring to four rounds of negotiations over the past 18 months, Baqeri said Tehran believed the United States had derailed each round through hostile actions and breaches of commitments. “We must see practical actions on the part of the Americans,” he said, describing such steps as necessary before a new chapter in diplomacy could begin. Baqeri also discussed Iran’s cooperation with Russia, saying a recent visit by Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei to Moscow was intended to convey a message from Iran’s leader to President Vladimir Putin.

items.title: Iran warns missile response to new attack could extend to Europe
items.summary: Iran warns missile response to new attack could extend to Europe An Iranian lawmaker has warned that any new US or Israeli attack could prompt missile strikes reaching Europe, adding that the response could push oil prices above $150 a barrel. “The range of the responding missiles will also encompass Europe, and this will lead to the oil price crossing the $150 threshold,” Hosseinali Haji Deligani, a member of parliament, told Iran’s Tasnim news agency. He said Iran’s response would be “massive, multiplied and strategic”, without geographical limits. Haji Deligani also described the US naval blockade of Iran as “a form of war”, warning that Iranian forces would attack “at the appropriate moment”. On Tuesday, Iran’s top military commander warned that the country’s armed forces would respond to any threat without “geographical limits”.

In many respects, the parallels between the 1974 midterms and the results of Tuesday’s election are eerie. De grootste veranderingen zijn te zien onder jonge kiezers, mannelijke kiezers, Latino-kiezers en mensen met de middelbare school als hoogste opleidingsniveau. The shades and nuances in each race were always going to be important this year, with expectations that many Republican supporters wouldn’t turn out for their party because of specific issues, such as inflation, fuel prices, the Iran war, datacentres, or Donald Trump’s toxicity. items.title: Iranian navy reports tanker on fire in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Iranian navy reports tanker on fire in Strait of Hormuz The Iranian navy reports that an "offending tanker" attempting to cross an "unsafe area" in the Strait of Hormuz has caught fire after hitting a mine. In comments carried by Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency, the Iranian authorities said that the vessel had halted its journey after the collision, adding that the tanker had “turned off its detection and navigation systems”. The statement warned that Tehran is “announcing to ship owners for the umpteenth time that the Strait of Hormuz is unsafe and closed to illegal vessels that intend to transit without coordination”.

items.summary: It has long been claimed that Americans do not vote based on foreign policy, but the results of Tuesday’s midterm elections demonstrated the limits of this truism, with a large majority of voters rejecting the Iran War waged by the Trump administration. Even before the election, an October Fox News poll indicated that the Iran war and issues associated with it (inflation and gas prices) were among the top issues voters were concerned about. Exit polling published by NBC News showed 74% of voters saw the Iran war as a “crucial” or “major factor” in their vote, while 62% believed using force against Iran was the wrong decision. This apparently has come as a nasty surprise to the war’s biggest defenders and surrogates, who had assured their followers that this backlash would not happen. Some have admitted their errors, but many have not, and that split has rapidly produced a circular firing squad, with neocons aggressively turning on those in their ranks who have conceded the war was a mistake. The Democrats secured a sweeping midterm election victory on Tuesday, but one critical question remains unresolved: is US President Donald Trump now more or less likely to resume the war on Iran with the election cycle over? Before the midterms, the US appeared to be on the verge of launching a new, wide-scale attack against Iran. The families of US diplomats were evacuated from the region, and additional US military assets flooded into the Middle East. Arab leaders issued cryptic warnings about a devastating new conflict. But the attack many diplomats and analysts expected around election day never materialised. In fact, Republicans are now blaming the Iran war, and even Israel, for their blistering defeat at the hands of the Democrats. Trump said on Wednesday that "it's largely true" the Iran war and high fuel prices tied to the conflict led to his party’s historic defeat. items.summary: US issues fresh sanctions against individuals and entities aiding Iran The US Treasury issued fresh sanctions on Wednesday targeting what it called "the vast criminal network" of companies and individuals tied to Iran. It named Indian nationals Suniel Kumar Sharma and his wife, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, as well as two other Indian citizens who head two of the couple's businesses, and nine separate entities connected to Sharma. "Their schemes have provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels involved in transporting Iranian petroleum, including vessels operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies," the department said in a statement. The department also sanctioned Turkey-based Fugo Group Services Inc for its ongoing support of Iran's heavily sanctioned aviation sector.

items.summary: De Amerikaanse president Trump is flink afgestraft in de tussentijdse verkiezingen, de midterms. De Democraten krijgen door de blauwe tsunami nu zowel een meerderheid in het Huis als de Senaat. Wat betekent deze gigantische overwinning van de Democraten voor Donald Trump? Luister hier: Deze aflevering van De Dag luister je via NPO Luister en alle andere podcastapps. Bevalt het? Vergeet je dan niet te abonneren. Amerikakenner en jurist Kenneth Manusama legt in podcast De Dag uit wat de Democraten kunnen met die meerderheid. Want de wensen zijn duidelijk: Amerika moet betaalbaarder worden, de Iran-oorlog moet stoppen en de inzet van ICE-agenten moet veranderen. President Trump dreigde direct om z'n veto in te zetten, als het volgens hem de verkeerde kant op gaat. Maar Trump moet ook oppassen dat de Republikeinse partij wel achter hem blijft staan. Reageren? items.summary: Een blue wave is over Amerika gespoeld. De Democraten hebben zowel de meerderheid in de Senaat als het Huis van Afgevaardigden behaald. In januari worden de nieuwe leden beëdigd en de Democraten hebben grootse plannen om Trump in de laatste twee jaar van zijn presidentschap te dwarsbomen. Wat kunnen de Democraten eigenlijk doen als ze straks het Congres domineren? Eerst een stapje terug, want wat doet het Congres precies? Het Congres bestaat uit het Huis van Afgevaardigden en de Senaat. De 435 leden van het Huis stemmen over wetgeving, kunnen onderzoeken starten en documenten opvragen. Ook heeft het Huis de macht over de portemonnee. Alles wat uit de schatkist wordt gehaald, moet langs het Huis. Dan de Senaat, die bevestigt de benoeming van kabinetsleden, ambassadeurs en rechters, waaronder die van het Hooggerechtshof. Een meerderheid in de Senaat kan Trumps genomineerden blokkeren. Bezuinigingen terugdraaien Democratische leider Hakeem Jeffries heeft vandaag grote plannen aangekondigd, onder meer het terugdraaien van de bezuinigingen op gezondheidszorg door de Big Beautiful Bill . clusters.headline: Usa, gli scanner respingono le schede elettorali: cosa è successo a New York

items.title: Usa, gli scanner respingono le schede elettorali: cosa è successo a New York
items.summary: Problemi agli scanner elettorali nella contea di Westchester, nello Stato di New York, durante le elezioni di Midterm. In numerosi seggi le macchine non sono riuscite a leggere le schede cartacee, restituendole agli elettori, come si vede nelle immagini girate a Yonkers. Per permettere la prosecuzione delle votazioni, i funzionari elettorali hanno disposto la raccolta delle schede in appositi sacchi di sicurezza, destinati al successivo conteggio. Secondo le autorità elettorali dello Stato, il problema è stato causato da un aggiornamento della programmazione degli scanner, che non erano in grado di riconoscere le schede utilizzate. Il responsabile dell'amministrazione della contea, Ken Jenkins, ha definito l'accaduto «completamente inaccettabile» e annunciato una verifica bipartisan per chiarire le cause del malfunzionamento. Le autorità hanno invitato i cittadini a continuare a votare, assicurando che tutte le schede valide sarebbero state conteggiate. Il guasto ha interessato anche i seggi di una circoscrizione contesa tra il repubblicano Mike Lawler e la democratica Cait Conley. ►

clusters.headline: MAGA: Why Trump's most loyal supporters are turning against him?

items.title: MAGA: Why Trump's most loyal supporters are turning against him?
items.summary:
Is Trump losing the support of the very coalition that brought him back to power?
 
Just one day before the midterm elections, Trump's approval rating stands at 32%, one of the lowest ever recorded at this stage of a presidency.
 
And discontent is growing beyond Democratic voters. Some of Trump's most loyal Republican and MAGA supporters are increasingly torn between political loyalty and economic reality. The war in Iran, rising costs linked to the Strait of Hormuz blockade, unfulfilled “America First” promises and other controversial issues, including the Epstein files scandal, are widening the rift between Trump and his electoral base.
 
Can he regain control of the diverse coalition that makes up MAGA?

clusters.headline: Heading into the midterms, 'no US president in recent times has been as unpopular as Donald Trump'

items.title: Heading into the midterms, 'no US president in recent times has been as unpopular as Donald Trump'
items.summary: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Richard Johnson, Senior Lecturer in US Politics at Queen Mary University of London. He says that "Donald Trump is damaged goods at this point in his presidency." With this uncompromising assessment, Johnson takes us through the political forces shaping the 2026 US midterm elections. Far from assuming that Trump's formidable campaigning instincts can once again mobilize Republican voters, Johnson questions whether the president's political influence has become a liability for the very party he once transformed. He points to a potentially significant realignment within the American electorate. Economic grievances, rising living costs, trade disputes and disillusionment with the war in Iran appear, in Johnson's reading, to be weakening important elements of the coalition that sustained Trump's return to power. Particularly consequential is the possibility that Latino voters, agricultural communities and sections of the MAGA electorate may be reconsidering their political loyalties or withdrawing from electoral participation altogether.

Donald Trump has the lowest approval rating of any US president going into a midterm election since Harry Truman. And it’s still dropping. The Democrats are projected to win by a margin of 11 percentage points , the largest swing by any party in almost 20 years. Many rural homes have an open fire or wood burner, but most rely on kerosene oil for hot water and heating. Since the US-Iran war began, its cost has more than doubled. Currently, 1,000 litres (lasting 10-12 weeks) is £1,219. A year ago, it was £549. Seasoned wood is in demand. clusters.headline: Piraten kapen Iraans schip bij Somalië, mogelijk met meer aanvallen als doel

items.title: Piraten kapen Iraans schip bij Somalië, mogelijk met meer aanvallen als doel
items.summary: Somalische piraten hebben een Iraans vissersschip aangevallen en overmeesterd. Er zijn 23 bemanningsleden aan boord van het schip. Dat meldt de EU-missie die moet bijdragen aan de veiligheid op de West-Indische Oceaan en de Rode Zee. Het schip werd donderdag gekaapt ten noordoosten van Somalië, tussen de kustplaatsen Bandar Bayla en Hafun. Volgens het veiligheidscentrum zijn de piraten gewapend en is onduidelijk hoe de bemanning het maakt. De EU-missie waarschuwt dat het schip mogelijk als uitvalsbasis wordt gebruikt voor meer piraterij. Het nadert een commerciële scheepvaartroute, volgens de laatst bekende positie. Twaalf piraten Een medewerker van de maritieme politie van Puntland zegt tegen persbureau AP dat er twaalf piraten aan boord zijn gegaan van het Iraanse schip, de Azini. Op het schip waren 21 Iraniërs en twee Somalische beveiligers. De EU-missie onderzoekt het incident. Schepen in de buurt zijn opgeroepen alert te zijn op verdachte situaties en die onmiddellijk te melden. Meer kapingen De afgelopen maanden zijn er nog vijf piratenaanvallen geweest voor de kust van Somalië

clusters.headline: Houthis repeat threats against Saudi oil giant, aviation

items.title: Houthis repeat threats against Saudi oil giant, aviation
items.summary: Houthis repeat threats against Saudi oil giant, aviation Houthi media, citing an anonymous military official, on Sunday repeated threats against Saudi oil giant Aramco and aviation in the kingdom. Yemen's Houthis, fighting a Saudi-led coalition backing the internationally recognised government, are allies of Iran, which on Sunday warned the US and Israel not to renew strikes on the Islamic Republic after they had threatened a return to war. "Aramco facilities are within range of the Yemeni Armed Forces, and investments in them are a venture fraught with losses," the Houthis' Saba news agency quoted the military official as saying. The official also warned international airlines against using Saudi airspace "except for the airspaces of Mecca and Medina".

items.title: Iran submits evidence of US-Israeli attacks on maritime infrastructure to IMO
items.summary: Iran submits evidence of US-Israeli attacks on maritime infrastructure to IMO Iran said it has submitted evidence of US and Israeli attacks on its maritime infrastructure to the International Maritime Organisation (IMO). The dossier of evidence given by Tehran to the IMO includes documents and photographic evidence of sabotage on its maritime infrastructure. An Iranian official said IMO member states will discuss the evidence at a council session taking place in London on 2-6 November. The attacks on its maritime infrastructure, according to Iran, threaten the safety of international shipping and seafarers. Iran's IRNA news agency reported that damage to maritime traffic control systems also increases the risk of accidents, and the destruction of rescue facilities undermines emergency response capabilities.

items.summary: Van Alaska en Texas tot grote delen van het Amerikaanse midwesten; drie keer op rij wist Donald Trump er zonder al te veel moeite te winnen. Toch lijken dieprode Republikeinse staten nu Democratisch blauw te kunnen kleuren. In de laatste dagen voor de Congres-verkiezingen moeten Republikeinen alle zeilen bijzetten. "Dit zijn de cruciaalste verkiezingen van ons leven", zegt Ashley Hinson, Congreslid voor de Republikeinen. Ze hoopt een vrijkomende senaatszetel namens Iowa te claimen. Er is geen zekerheid: in de peilingen gaat ze nek aan nek met haar Democratische tegenkandidaat. "Wie heeft er al gestemd?" vraagt Hinson aan de mensen in een motelzaaltje in Coralville. Het merendeel van de vijftig aanwezigen steekt de hand omhoog. Op de meeste hier kan ze rekenen. Het motel ligt aan de I-80, de snelweg die de west- en oostkust van de VS met elkaar verbindt. New York en San Francisco, het begin- en eindpunt van de snelweg, zijn blauw: daar wordt steevast Democratisch gestemd. items.title: Iran could revisit nuclear weapons ban if war resumes, security chief says
items.summary: Iran could revisit nuclear weapons ban if war resumes, security chief says Iran is debating whether to maintain its longstanding ban on nuclear weapons if hostilities resume, though no decision has been taken on any change, Iranian Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei told state media on Saturday. Rezaei also said Washington's tone had shifted as it sought to restart negotiations with the Islamic Republic. The US Vice President JD Vance wrote to Rezaei last week in a bid to revive diplomacy. According to the New York Times, Qatari mediators handed the letter to Rezaei. It proposed direct talks headed by Vance, with Iran's nuclear programme up for discussion from the outset. "I read the letter. I haven’t yet responded. Their tone has completely changed," Rezaei said, calling the shift "a good sign" that showed Iran had "consolidated its victory". He declined to comment further on the letter's contents, but said Iran's nuclear issue could be discussed only after the United States met Iran's demands. clusters.headline: Khamenei orders immediate response to any threat 'without geographical limitations'

items.title: Khamenei orders immediate response to any threat 'without geographical limitations'
items.summary: Khamenei orders immediate response to any threat 'without geographical limitations' Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has ordered the country’s armed forces to deliver an "immediate, effective response without geographical limitations" to any potential enemy threat, according to the state news agency IRNA. In directives issued after a meeting with senior military commanders, Khamenei called for “intelligent combat readiness” to ensure what he described as “maximum deterrence”. He also ordered an update to Iran’s “Targets Bank” to bring tangible and intangible US and Israeli assets within the reach of Iranian forces. Khamenei further called for strengthening Iran’s military information systems, developing domestic defence capabilities and incorporating new technologies into its security and military infrastructure. “If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for their end,” he said.

items.title: Trump vs MAGA: Why his movement is splitting
items.summary:
As the 2026 midterm elections approach, divisions within the MAGA camp are becoming increasingly visible. From the war in Iran and rising fuel prices to the Epstein files, several of Trump’s decisions are fuelling divisions among his most loyal supporters.
 
Once united by a shared vision of America, MAGA now brings together factions that increasingly disagree over foreign policy, the economy and what “America First” should actually mean. Yet Trump remains the central figure holding this political coalition together – and he is fighting to keep it that way.
 
Why are some of the president’s longtime allies distancing themselves from him? Can MAGA remain united despite these disagreements? And can Trump still mobilise his base ahead of the midterms?
 
🔍 Our journalist Stella Elgersma breaks down the divisions within the MAGA movement and Donald Trump’s strategy to rally his supporters, once again.

items.summary: Oil spills from tankers attacked by Iran in Hormuz reach UAE coastline, report says Oil spills from tankers attacked by Iran near the Strait of Hormuz have reached the UAE coastline, prompting beach closures in three emirates and raising concerns about marine life, the Financial Times reported. The first spill to reach the coast left dark slicks along beaches, with authorities closing affected areas in Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah. The UAE environment ministry said it was coordinating cleanup operations and urged fishermen to avoid polluted areas. Marine monitor Windward recorded 12 spills between July and September, including one that spread across an area of 2,000 square kilometres off Oman. Satellite imagery also showed an oil slick near Ras Al Khaimah. Experts warned that turtles, dolphins, seabirds and other marine species could be affected. Authorities have not identified the leaking vessel, but marine security experts cited by the FT said it was the Chinese-owned supertanker Gem No. 2, hit off Sharjah more than two weeks ago. items.title: Palestinian journalist returns home after 15 months in Israeli detention
items.summary: Palestinian journalist returns home after 15 months in Israeli detention Palestinian journalist Farah Abu Ayyash has returned home to her family following 450 days of detention in Israeli prisons, according to a report by the Islamic Republic News Agency (Irna). Abu Ayyash, a West Bank correspondent for Iran's Tasnim News Agency, was freed on Thursday night after the Ofer Prison military court ordered her release, dismissing the charges brought against her after she served 15 months under administrative detention. According to Irna, Abu Ayyash was initially detained on 6 August 2025, during an overnight military raid on her family home in Beit Ummar, north of Hebron. The outlet reported that her arrest was tied to her journalistic work covering local developments across the southern West Bank for Tasnim. The report further noted that repeated procedural delays prolonged her case, keeping her detained without formal resolution under administrative detention at Damon Prison. Irna also reported that the correspondent was allegedly subjected to torture and mistreatment while in custody.

A total of 277 vessel transits were recorded in the strait during the seven days to October 28, comprising 155 inbound and 122 outbound movements. The combined figure, which includes automatic identification system (AIS) observations and US-reported facilitated transits, was approximately 70 percent below pre-conflict levels. UKMTO said AIS-observed transits increased to 64 from 47 the previous week, while US-reported facilitated movements remained broadly stable. items.summary: Merz says Germany working to end Iran war that has cost Europe $112bn German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has said that Germany was working to bring Iran war to an end as soon as possible as the conflict has added more than 100 billion euros ($112bn) to Europe’s energy costs over the past eight months. Speaking to reporters in Seoul on Friday, he said Germany was coordinating and stepping up diplomatic efforts to bring the conflict to an end, while stressing that the "conflict cannot be resolved militarily". “Businesses and consumers in Europe have paid more than 100 billion euros extra because energy has become more expensive as a result of this conflict,” he said. “We therefore also have an economic interest in bringing this conflict to an end as quickly as possible.”

items.title: Iran slams Canada for supporting UAE claim over three Gulf islands
items.summary: Iran slams Canada for supporting UAE claim over three Gulf islands Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei has criticised Canada's support for the United Arab Emirates' claim to three Gulf islands, questioning Ottawa's commitment to territorial integrity and national sovereignty. In a post on X, Baqaei said the UAE, established in 1971, was laying claim to Abu Musa and the Greater Tunb and Lesser Tunb despite "historical records and geographical and documented evidence establishing their Iranian ownership". He said the islands had been part of Iran for millennia, long before the UAE federation was established, and criticised Canada's prime minister for echoing what he called an “absurd claim”. Baqaei invoked Canada's own history of defending its sovereignty, citing the American invasion during the War of 1812, the Montreal Annexation Manifesto of 1849 and US President Donald Trump's repeated remarks about making Canada the 51st US state. “How can it take sides in a fabricated dispute and endorse an unfounded territorial claim that amounts to dangerous adventurism?” he said.

items.summary: De traditionele groepsfoto op de G20-top in de Verenigde Staten is niet doorgegaan vanwege de aanwezigheid van de Russische minister Lavrov van Buitenlandse Zaken. De Amerikaanse regering besloot om het fotomoment maar te schrappen, omdat andere aanwezigen met een boycot dreigden. Delegaties van een aantal landen die achter Oekraïne staan, waaronder Canada en Australië, wilden in Atlanta niet met Sergej Lavrov op de 'familiefoto', het kiekje met alle deelnemers aan een top. Een aantal delegaties dreigde zelfs weg te lopen, schrijft de Amerikaanse nieuwszender CNN . Europese functionarissen dachten nog dat er mogelijk twee aparte foto's zouden worden gemaakt, een met Lavrov en een zonder hem. Toen dat niet geval bleek besloot de Amerikaanse minister van Buitenlandse Zaken er maar van af te zien, omdat hij niet wilde dat de top overschaduwd zou worden door een foto-rel, zeggen betrokken Amerikaanse diplomaten tegen persbureau AP. items.title: Oman evacuates crew of tanker set ablaze near Hormuz
items.summary: Oman evacuates crew of tanker set ablaze near Hormuz Oman said on Friday it had rescued 25 sailors from a merchant ship that was targeted and set ablaze, as Iran reported three oil tankers had been halted while crossing the blockaded Strait of Hormuz. Muscat’s navy “carried out an evacuation operation for 25 crew members of the merchant ship Riti, flying the Panamanian flag, after it was targeted, which led to a fire breaking out on board”, Oman’s Maritime Security Centre said in a statement. The crew members were provided with medical care, the Omani statement said. The MarineTraffic ship-tracking website described the Riti as a crude oil tanker. In a video released earlier on Friday, Centcom chief Brad Cooper said US forces had “successfully cleared the strait’s internationally recognised primary transit routes of Iranian sea mines”. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps said separately that three oil tankers had been halted after encountering unspecified “incidents” or hitting mines.

In a video posted on Cencom's X account, Cooper said he flew over the strait earlier this week and saw dozens of commercial vessels transiting the area. “Here’s what I didn’t see: I didn’t see the IRGC out there at all,” he said, claiming Iran’s navy was “all at the bottom of the sea”. The remarks come as Iran has repeatedly claimed that it maintains control over the strait. Earlier, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it had stopped two tankers attempting to cross the southern part of the waterway, accusing them of using “unauthorised routes” with US military support.

In a statement, the IRGC Navy said the vessels, one in the eastern and the other in the western part of the strait, had switched off their navigation and positioning systems and ignored several radio warnings. The IRGC Navy also said another vessel that caught fire in the southern waters of the strait on Thursday night had sunk.

clusters.headline: Old News: After 26-year rule, Shah of Iran crowns himself ‘King of Kings’

items.title: Old News: After 26-year rule, Shah of Iran crowns himself ‘King of Kings’
items.summary: Old News is a new initiative by Amwaj.media to connect the past to the present. Through “reporting” on pivotal moments in history, we aim to provide a richer backdrop for current dynamics in the region. The story: Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi has crowned himself Iran’s “King of Kings,” and his wife as Empress. The event took place at a lavish ceremony in Tehran's Golestan Palace, 26 years after becoming head of state. Observers say Pahlavi has delayed his coronation to await the birth of a male heir, and to initiate enough progress and reform in Iran to legitimize his rule. The coronation has drawn national and international praise for reforms implemented as part of the Shah’s “White Revolution,” though he is also facing domestic criticism for his policies and autocratic rule. items.summary: Al maanden stijgen de prijzen voor olie en gas door de oorlog in het Midden-Oosten. Grote energieconcerns lijden daar niet onder, blijkt vandaag uit cijfers. Terwijl de bedrijven hoge winsten behalen, blijven de energietarieven voor consumenten alsmaar oplopen. En dat levert de vraag op: kun je het beste een vast, variabel of toch dynamisch contract afsluiten? Verschillende energiebedrijven maakten de torenhoge winsten bekend die ze de afgelopen drie maanden hebben gemaakt. Zo zagen Shell en Vattenfall hun winst verdubbelen door de hoge olie- en gasprijs. Ondertussen kwam de gasprijs voor een megawattuur gisteren voor het eerst sinds het najaar van 2022 boven de 100 euro uit. De stijgende gasrekening leidt tot vragen bij de Consumentenbond. "Heel veel vragen van mensen over wat ze moeten doen. Het leeft ontzettend", zegt Joyce Donat van de Consumentenbond. Ook consumentencollectief United Consumers ziet dat klanten op zoek zijn naar antwoorden en zekerheid. Toch is er geen pasklaar antwoord. Vast contract "Tot voor kort loonde het om een vast contract af te sluiten net voor de zomer.

The higher energy prices that have resulted from the Iran war have pushed up inflation, are eating into households’ incomes, are a drag on businesses – and are the main reason why the forecast for GDP growth next year was cut from 1.6% to just 1%. The Trump administration’s diplomatic push against the annual resolution — spearheaded by U.S. Ambassador to the U.N. Mike Waltz — has been even more intense than last year’s . While the pressure failed to defeat the measure, it created a notable shift in the vote tally. clusters.headline: The Legacy of Reykjavik and the Future of U.S.–Russia Nuclear Relations

items.title: The Legacy of Reykjavik and the Future of U.S.–Russia Nuclear Relations
items.summary: On 11-12 October 1986, U.S. President Ronald Reagan and Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev met in Reykjavik, Iceland, hoping to achieve a groundbreaking agreement on controlling the world’s most dangerous weapons. While the summit yielded no agreement, it set in motion arms control negotiations tracks, held up the promise of nuclear disarmament, and contributed to the transformation of relations between two Cold War ach-adversaries. Forty years on, what lessons does Reykjavik hold for arms control, disarmament, and great power relations? To discuss the legacy of Reykjavik, Project on Managing the Atom (MTA) is honored to welcome Pavel Palazhchenko, former interpreter of Mikhail Gorbachev and an ambassador of the Gorbachev Foundation, David Holloway, Professor Emeritus of Stanford University and author of the International History of Nuclear Weapons, Matthew Bunn, Professor at Harvard Kennedy School, and Carol Saivetz, Senior Fellow at MIT Security Studies Program, with Mariana Budjeryn, MTA associate and a senior researcher at MIT as moderator.

items.title: Voormalig Midden-Oostencorrespondent Thomas Loudon (56) overleden
items.summary: Journalist en oud-correspondent Thomas Loudon is overleden. Hij kampte met neuro-endocriene tumoren (NET), een langzaam groeiende vorm van kanker. Vorig jaar kreeg hij de diagnose en deze week overleed hij daaraan. Hij was 56 jaar. In 2001 werd Loudon de eerste Nederlandse (video)journalist die zich na de Islamitische Revolutie in Iran vestigde. Hij deed in diverse talen verslag van ontwikkelingen in Iran, Afghanistan en het noorden van Irak voor onder meer de NOS, Trouw en Elsevier, maar ook voor buitenlandse media als CNN, het Chileense Canal 13 en Asia TV in Singapore. Egypte en Jordanië In 2003 trok hij naar de Egyptische hoofdstad Caïro, waar hij Midden-Oostencorrespondent werd voor de NOS. Daarna deed hij dat vanuit Jordanië. Hij maakte onder meer verhalen over de Amerikaanse oorlog in Irak. Correspondent bleef hij tot begin 2007, waarna hij terugkeerde naar Nederland. In de jaren daarna was hij actief als docent journalistiek in Groningen en Rotterdam. Ook richtte hij zijn eigen organisatie op om journalisten te ondersteunen in landen waar de persvrijheid onder druk staat. Daa

After two years of President Donald Trump's tariffs, threats to annex Greenland and scolding of European NATO allies on defense spending, many European politicians see the Republican defeat as a welcome course correction. Yet the reactions also expose the contradictions of the European Union’s own foreign policy, particularly toward the wars in Iran and Ukraine. items.title: Freezer meltdowns and airline hoaxes are a taste of things to come. Hoping for the best is no longer an option | Elisabeth Braw
items.summary: Acts of greyzone aggression aim to spread panic. Europe has to show the saboteurs that we are resilient It was as though a ghostly hand had switched the settings on supermarket freezers across Europe from “freeze” to “defrost”. From Finland to Ireland, they suddenly began heating up , many reaching 50C and food worth millions of euros had to be thrown away. But no actual hand was needed to cause the meltdown. This was a cyber-attack, or rather a chain of attacks. Like pretty much everything else in 2026, supermarket freezers are digitally enabled. That makes them smarter and more efficient, but like everything else that is connected to the internet, it also makes them more vulnerable. Russian hacktivists claimed they were behind some of the supermarket sabotage, but no one knows for sure. It could also be Iran, Iranian proxies, North Korea – or unaffiliated bedroom hackers. When Transport for London suffered a devastating hack two years ago, the culprits turned out to be two British teenagers . items.title: Iranian forces on higher alert, stronger than before war, spokesman says
items.summary: Iranian forces on higher alert, stronger than before war, spokesman says Iran's military is "stronger" and more motivated than it was when the United States and Israel started the war in February, says Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia. "Today, the Islamic Republic's armed forces... having gained experience from direct confrontation with the United States and the Israeli regime, are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war," Akraminia said, according to the state news agency Irna. "They now possess greater motivation, commitment, and self-confidence." Akraminia said that Iranian armed forces retained control over the Strait of Hormuz and that it would remain closed until the United States accepted Tehran's demands. "Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective, and without geographical limitations," he added.

items.title: Trump says US knocked out Iranian 'little bit of anti-aircraft device'
items.summary: Trump says US knocked out Iranian 'little bit of anti-aircraft device' US President Donald Trump says Washington had made considerable progress in its dealings with Iran, while acknowledging that US forces had carried out limited strikes against targets on the country. "I don't want to talk about it. We do minor strikes. But they knocked out... and they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device. And we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five," Trump told reporters when asked about reports of strikes near Iran's Qeshm Island. Speaking to reporters after arriving aboard Air Force One at Donald J. Trump International Airport, Trump said the United States was taking out more Iranian oil than before the conflict. "We've made a lot of progress with Iran, we're taking out more oil now than we were before the war. It's not a war," he said. "You know, in Russia-Ukraine, they lose 25,000 people a month. Eight attacks occurred in the Strait of Hormuz and three in the Arabian Gulf, according to UKMTO's weekly overview. Of the 11 incidents, three vessels continued their voyages, five required assistance and three sank. The report said one dhow was struck by an unidentified projectile on 2 November, killing one crew member, while 13 others were rescued by local authorities. A Panama-flagged supply vessel was also struck by an unidentified projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on 1 November and reportedly sank after a nearby merchant vessel rescued its crew. A Marshall Islands-flagged tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles in the Arabian Gulf on 4 November, leaving it drifting and requiring assistance from local authorities. A State Department programme, Rewards for Justice, "is offering a reward of up to $20 million and possible relocation for information about Iran's nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community," US Central Command said on X. The programme was established in 1984 under the State Department's national security rewards programme to offer money for information that protects American lives and interests. In its statement about the reward, the State Department said Iran's "lack of compliance with the IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency) on safeguards obligations" has led to the agency's loss of 'continuity of knowledge' regarding Iran's production and inventory of key components like centrifuges. items.title: US issues new Iran sanctions as Trump says talks with Tehran going 'very well'
items.summary: US issues new Iran sanctions as Trump says talks with Tehran going 'very well' US President Donald Trump said on Friday that his administration was in talks with Iranian representatives, telling reporters: "We are doing very well with Iran." His comments came as the US Treasury Department imposed new Iran-related sanctions on eight entities based in Canada, according to a notice on its website. In a separate move on Friday, the Treasury blocked US banks from dealing with MEXC Global, a cryptocurrency exchange registered in the Seychelles. It accused the exchange of handling at least $16bn in illegal transactions linked to Iran, North Korea and Russia, helping them get around sanctions. On Thursday, the Treasury sanctioned companies and individuals in India and Turkey that it accused of helping Iran evade restrictions on its oil exports and airlines. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the same day that Washington would continue to pursue anyone supporting Tehran. items.summary: US and Iran edge closer to potential breakthrough in talks to end war, Bloomberg reports The United States and Iran are moving closer to a possible breakthrough in efforts to end the war, with Tehran considering proposals on its nuclear programme that it had previously been unwilling to discuss, Bloomberg reported, citing a diplomat familiar with the talks. The diplomat said Iran was studying proposals on its nuclear activities presented by Qatar, the main mediator. Any concession could help to advance negotiations, which have stalled since the collapse of an interim agreement reached in June. Reuters and The New York Times have also previously reported on Iran’s willingness to compromise on the nuclear issue. US President Donald Trump spoke by phone with Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani about efforts to de-escalate the conflict and secure a comprehensive agreement, the emir’s office said on Friday. Qatari officials have been shuttling between Doha and Tehran to help bridge differences, including over Iran’s nuclear activities and the US naval blockade of Iranian ports.

In the 2022 midterms, Aipac’s Super Pac, United Democracy Project, saw 69 percent of its expenditure spent on races backed by the organisation that won. items.title: Election was a check on Trump — and Biden — foreign policy
items.summary: There is no debate as to why Donald Trump and the Republican Party suffered a historic and humiliating defeat at the polls on Tuesday: it all comes down to the Iran war and the cost-of-living crisis it has brought about. But lost in the conversation is that this was not just a rejection of the Iran war. It was also a repudiation of the broader foreign policy that repeatedly gets the U.S. into wars — or into supporting the wars and war crimes of U.S. partners. In many contests on Tuesday, the U.S.-Israel relationship was on the ballot too, and it was rejected by Republicans and Democrats alike in favor of recentering priorities back to national interests, including ending the flow of military aid to Israel. Trump famously ran on a promise to end forever wars and not to start new ones. items.title: AIPAC dumped more than $55 million into losing midterm races
items.summary: The largest pro-Israel group in the U.S., the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC), has been silent on social media since Tuesday afternoon, well before polls closed across the country and Democrats won both chambers of Congress in a blue wave, largely driven by dissatisfaction over rising costs sparked by the war in Iran. The group was an early supporter of the war and a major funder of ads attacking House and Senate candidates calling to cut off aid to Israel. It spent big on the 2026 midterm elections, dumping $84.1 million via its super PAC, United Democracy Project (UDP), and several other PACs into races that have been decided as of this writing. AIPAC might be silent today because they need to explain to their donors how nearly-two-thirds, or $55.3 million, of that spending went to races in which the group’s preferred candidate lost. items.title: US issues fresh sanctions against individuals and entities aiding Iran
items.summary: US issues fresh sanctions against individuals and entities aiding Iran The US Treasury issued fresh sanctions on Wednesday targeting what it called "the vast criminal network" of companies and individuals tied to Iran. It named Indian nationals Suniel Kumar Sharma and his wife, Jaspreet Preeti Shahid, as well as two other Indian citizens who head two of the couple's businesses, and nine separate entities connected to Sharma. "Their schemes have provided false flags and certifications to sanctioned vessels involved in transporting Iranian petroleum, including vessels operating on behalf of the Iranian military and its proxies," the department said in a statement. The department also sanctioned Turkey-based Fugo Group Services Inc for its ongoing support of Iran's heavily sanctioned aviation sector.

items.title: Trump admits Iran war caused election losses but ‘we had to do it’
items.summary: Trump admits Iran war caused election losses but ‘we had to do it’ US President Donald Trump said on Wednesday that the Iran war was responsible for his Republican Party's resounding midterm election defeat. Asked whether he agreed with Vice President JD Vance earlier remarks that the Iran war was "the reason we lost", Trump told reporters outside the White House ballroom construction site that his comments were "largely true because it drove the gasoline up a little bit short term". "But at the same time, if I had it to do again, I'd have to do it again. Because long term, it's the only answer. You can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon," he added. He also ruled out firing Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, saying "he's doing a very good job," despite his role in pushing for military action against Tehran. US President Donald Trump speaks to reporters before the construction site of the East Wing ballroom at the White House in Washington, DC, on 4 November 2026 (Mandel Ngan/AFP)

items.title: Tale of 2 midterms: Republican redistricting 'backfired' while Democrats 'exceeded all expectations'
items.summary: Following a resounding Midterm election defeat, Is MAGA Losing Its Grip on the Republican Party? Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Bryan Lanza, Republican strategist and Partner in Mercury's Washington DC office. "The big thing about MAGA was confrontation, in your face," explained Lanza. But following a veritable blue wave, he believes the electorate has delivered a warning: "We need to move beyond that." While Donald Trump has acknowledged the Democratic victory, at times combative, at times conciliatory, Lanza argues that the president must begin his final two years in office reversing damaging tariffs, addressing widespread dissatisfaction with immigration enforcement and navigating a highly unpopular Iran war.

items.title: Podcast De Dag: de problemen van Trump
items.summary: De Amerikaanse president Trump is flink afgestraft in de tussentijdse verkiezingen, de midterms. De Democraten krijgen door de blauwe tsunami nu zowel een meerderheid in het Huis als de Senaat. Wat betekent deze gigantische overwinning van de Democraten voor Donald Trump? Luister hier: Deze aflevering van De Dag luister je via NPO Luister en alle andere podcastapps. Bevalt het? Vergeet je dan niet te abonneren. Amerikakenner en jurist Kenneth Manusama legt in podcast De Dag uit wat de Democraten kunnen met die meerderheid. Want de wensen zijn duidelijk: Amerika moet betaalbaarder worden, de Iran-oorlog moet stoppen en de inzet van ICE-agenten moet veranderen. President Trump dreigde direct om z'n veto in te zetten, als het volgens hem de verkeerde kant op gaat. Maar Trump moet ook oppassen dat de Republikeinse partij wel achter hem blijft staan. Reageren? Mail naar dedag@nos.nl Presentatie & montage: Marco Geijtenbeek Redactie: Rosanne Sies Eindredactie: Judith van de Hulsbeek

items.title: Epstein-files, afzetting of corruptie aanpakken, wat gaan Democraten doen met hun macht?
items.summary: Een blue wave is over Amerika gespoeld. De Democraten hebben zowel de meerderheid in de Senaat als het Huis van Afgevaardigden behaald. In januari worden de nieuwe leden beëdigd en de Democraten hebben grootse plannen om Trump in de laatste twee jaar van zijn presidentschap te dwarsbomen. Wat kunnen de Democraten eigenlijk doen als ze straks het Congres domineren? Eerst een stapje terug, want wat doet het Congres precies? Het Congres bestaat uit het Huis van Afgevaardigden en de Senaat. De 435 leden van het Huis stemmen over wetgeving, kunnen onderzoeken starten en documenten opvragen. Ook heeft het Huis de macht over de portemonnee. Alles wat uit de schatkist wordt gehaald, moet langs het Huis. Dan de Senaat, die bevestigt de benoeming van kabinetsleden, ambassadeurs en rechters, waaronder die van het Hooggerechtshof. Een meerderheid in de Senaat kan Trumps genomineerden blokkeren. items.title: Usa, gli scanner respingono le schede elettorali: cosa è successo a New York
items.summary: Problemi agli scanner elettorali nella contea di Westchester, nello Stato di New York, durante le elezioni di Midterm. In numerosi seggi le macchine non sono riuscite a leggere le schede cartacee, restituendole agli elettori, come si vede nelle immagini girate a Yonkers. Per permettere la prosecuzione delle votazioni, i funzionari elettorali hanno disposto la raccolta delle schede in appositi sacchi di sicurezza, destinati al successivo conteggio. Secondo le autorità elettorali dello Stato, il problema è stato causato da un aggiornamento della programmazione degli scanner, che non erano in grado di riconoscere le schede utilizzate. Il responsabile dell'amministrazione della contea, Ken Jenkins, ha definito l'accaduto «completamente inaccettabile» e annunciato una verifica bipartisan per chiarire le cause del malfunzionamento. Le autorità hanno invitato i cittadini a continuare a votare, assicurando che tutte le schede valide sarebbero state conteggiate. Il guasto ha interessato anche i seggi di una circoscrizione contesa tra il repubblicano Mike Lawler e la democratica Cait Conley. ►

items.title: Major losses could spur Trump to escalate war before year's end
items.summary: As much as the Iran war is the key reason Trump and the GOP were crushed tonight, it is important to recognize that the pressure for war is now likely to increase . This does not mean that Trump will restart the war. But the balance of pressure for and against war will likely favor escalation. Trump was under a degree of pressure to strike a deal before the midterms, hoping to soften the blow in the polls. But now that the midterms are over, that pressure will dissipate somewhat. Gas prices are still high, but the political cost has already been paid. There won’t be another point on the political calendar for some time when that cost can be exacted again. But two other factors will intensify. First, pro-war elements in Israel and in Washington will see the next two months as the last period in which Trump has wide maneuverability to restart the war. By January, the Democrats will control both chambers, will control the purse, and can begin impeaching Trump’s secretaries, including Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth. items.title: ‘It’s the war, stupid’: Dems sweep midterms on wave of voter anger
items.summary: Democrats secured an overwhelming victory in the midterm elections on Tuesday in a stunning rebuke to President Donald Trump’s first two years in office, winning majorities in both the Senate and House of Representatives. By midnight Democrats flipped six Senate seats — including in reliably red states like South Carolina, Texas, and Kansas. As of this morning, they added Michigan and Maine. In a rare inversion of historical trends, foreign policy played a serious role in the results of Tuesday’s midterm elections. Exit polling showed 74% of voters said the Iran War was a “crucial” or “major” factor in their vote. Exit polling also found that 62% of voters believed using military force against Iran was the “wrong decision.” This all jibed with polls leading up to the midterms. Gallup reported last week that 77% of registered voters considered the situation in Iran “extremely” or “very important” to their vote, placing it among the top issues surveyed, alongside the economy and healthcare. Just one day before the midterm elections, Trump's approval rating stands at 32%, one of the lowest ever recorded at this stage of a presidency.

The war in Iran, rising costs linked to the Strait of Hormuz blockade, unfulfilled “America First” promises and other controversial issues, including the Epstein files scandal, are widening the rift between Trump and his electoral base.
 
Can he regain control of the diverse coalition that makes up MAGA?
 
FRANCE 24 journalist Stella Elgersma spoke to MAGA and Republican experts to explore how the movement has evolved, what its supporters want and what is driving their discontent.

items.title: Heading into the midterms, 'no US president in recent times has been as unpopular as Donald Trump'
items.summary: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Richard Johnson, Senior Lecturer in US Politics at Queen Mary University of London. He says that "Donald Trump is damaged goods at this point in his presidency." With this uncompromising assessment, Johnson takes us through the political forces shaping the 2026 US midterm elections. Far from assuming that Trump's formidable campaigning instincts can once again mobilize Republican voters, Johnson questions whether the president's political influence has become a liability for the very party he once transformed. He points to a potentially significant realignment within the American electorate. Economic grievances, rising living costs, trade disputes and disillusionment with the war in Iran appear, in Johnson's reading, to be weakening important elements of the coalition that sustained Trump's return to power. Particularly consequential is the possibility that Latino voters, agricultural communities and sections of the MAGA electorate may be reconsidering their political loyalties or withdrawing from electoral participation altogether.

Hij had twaalf jaar bij de Britse luchtlandingstroepen gediend, waar hij zich enorm verveelde omdat het vredestijd was. Bushby kampte met angststoornissen en was bang voor de dood, zei hij deze maand tegen The Guardian . Het idee van een jarenlange wandeltocht liet hem niet los, hij wilde iets presteren. De twintiger stelde zichzelf twee doelen: hij mocht geen gemotoriseerd vervoer gebruiken en moest lopend zijn Britse geboorteplaats Hull zien te bereiken. items.title: These midterms could effectively end the Trump era – but neither side is yet ready for what comes next | Nesrine Malik
items.summary: Despite the US president’s ratings being at rock bottom, undoing his legacy will be difficult, not least because the Democrats are in disarray The stats and polling all suggest one thing: the Republicans are set for a hammering in the midterms. Donald Trump has the lowest approval rating of any US president going into a midterm election since Harry Truman. And it’s still dropping. The Democrats are projected to win by a margin of 11 percentage points , the largest swing by any party in almost 20 years. items.title: Iran warns new war could last longer after Trump threatens strikes
items.summary: Iran warns new war could last longer after Trump threatens strikes Iran warned on Sunday that any renewed war with the United States could last longer than the previous round of fighting, after President Donald Trump said he still had to "take care" of more targets. Diplomatic efforts to end the Middle East war have been punctuated by repeated threats from the US and Israel to resume bombardments as they hold crucial elections. "A potential future war could last longer than previous conflict, and the American president would not be in a position to dictate the timing or the conditions of its conclusion," said army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia, according to Iranian state television. Akraminia's remarks followed Trump's suggestion that the US could swiftly strike its remaining targets in Iran.

items.title: Piraten kapen Iraans schip bij Somalië, mogelijk met meer aanvallen als doel
items.summary: Somalische piraten hebben een Iraans vissersschip aangevallen en overmeesterd. Er zijn 23 bemanningsleden aan boord van het schip. Dat meldt de EU-missie die moet bijdragen aan de veiligheid op de West-Indische Oceaan en de Rode Zee. Het schip werd donderdag gekaapt ten noordoosten van Somalië, tussen de kustplaatsen Bandar Bayla en Hafun. Volgens het veiligheidscentrum zijn de piraten gewapend en is onduidelijk hoe de bemanning het maakt. De EU-missie waarschuwt dat het schip mogelijk als uitvalsbasis wordt gebruikt voor meer piraterij. Het nadert een commerciële scheepvaartroute, volgens de laatst bekende positie. Twaalf piraten Een medewerker van de maritieme politie van Puntland zegt tegen persbureau AP dat er twaalf piraten aan boord zijn gegaan van het Iraanse schip, de Azini. Op het schip waren 21 Iraniërs en twee Somalische beveiligers. De EU-missie onderzoekt het incident. Schepen in de buurt zijn opgeroepen alert te zijn op verdachte situaties en die onmiddellijk te melden. Meer kapingen De afgelopen maanden zijn er nog vijf piratenaanvallen geweest voor de kust van Somalië

items.title: Israel shells south Lebanon towns, builds roads connecting military outposts
items.summary: Israel shells south Lebanon towns, builds roads connecting military outposts Israeli forces carried out a large explosion in the town of Baraachit, in south Lebanon ’s Bint Jbeil district, on Saturday evening, Lebanon’s National News Agency (NNA) reported. Israeli artillery also shelled Beit Yahoun, in the same district, and the area between the towns of Zawtar al-Sharqiya and Maifadoun. An Israeli air strike hit the town of Mansouri, while Israeli warplanes flew low over the city of Tyre and its surroundings, staging mock raids. Alongside ongoing demolitions, the Israeli army has been building several roads through mountains and valleys in the western and central parts of south Lebanon, connecting the military outposts it set up after occupying the area, according to NNA. Israel sharply escalated its military operations in Lebanon this year, launching a ground invasion and occupying large parts of the country’s south and east. items.title: Rood of toch blauw? Republikeinen doen aan koorddansen om kiezers te behouden
items.summary: Van Alaska en Texas tot grote delen van het Amerikaanse midwesten; drie keer op rij wist Donald Trump er zonder al te veel moeite te winnen. Toch lijken dieprode Republikeinse staten nu Democratisch blauw te kunnen kleuren. In de laatste dagen voor de Congres-verkiezingen moeten Republikeinen alle zeilen bijzetten. "Dit zijn de cruciaalste verkiezingen van ons leven", zegt Ashley Hinson, Congreslid voor de Republikeinen. Ze hoopt een vrijkomende senaatszetel namens Iowa te claimen. Er is geen zekerheid: in de peilingen gaat ze nek aan nek met haar Democratische tegenkandidaat. "Wie heeft er al gestemd?" vraagt Hinson aan de mensen in een motelzaaltje in Coralville. Het merendeel van de vijftig aanwezigen steekt de hand omhoog. Op de meeste hier kan ze rekenen. Het motel ligt aan de I-80, de snelweg die de west- en oostkust van de VS met elkaar verbindt. New York en San Francisco, het begin- en eindpunt van de snelweg, zijn blauw: daar wordt steevast Democratisch gestemd. Rezaei also said Washington's tone had shifted as it sought to restart negotiations with the Islamic Republic. The US Vice President JD Vance wrote to Rezaei last week in a bid to revive diplomacy. According to the New York Times, Qatari mediators handed the letter to Rezaei. It proposed direct talks headed by Vance, with Iran's nuclear programme up for discussion from the outset. "I read the letter. I haven’t yet responded. Their tone has completely changed," Rezaei said, calling the shift "a good sign" that showed Iran had "consolidated its victory". items.title: Khamenei orders immediate response to any threat 'without geographical limitations'
items.summary: Khamenei orders immediate response to any threat 'without geographical limitations' Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has ordered the country’s armed forces to deliver an "immediate, effective response without geographical limitations" to any potential enemy threat, according to the state news agency IRNA. In directives issued after a meeting with senior military commanders, Khamenei called for “intelligent combat readiness” to ensure what he described as “maximum deterrence”. He also ordered an update to Iran’s “Targets Bank” to bring tangible and intangible US and Israeli assets within the reach of Iranian forces. Khamenei further called for strengthening Iran’s military information systems, developing domestic defence capabilities and incorporating new technologies into its security and military infrastructure. “If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for their end,” he said.

The first spill to reach the coast left dark slicks along beaches, with authorities closing affected areas in Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah. The UAE environment ministry said it was coordinating cleanup operations and urged fishermen to avoid polluted areas. Marine monitor Windward recorded 12 spills between July and September, including one that spread across an area of 2,000 square kilometres off Oman. Satellite imagery also showed an oil slick near Ras Al Khaimah. Experts warned that turtles, dolphins, seabirds and other marine species could be affected. Authorities have not identified the leaking vessel, but marine security experts cited by the FT said it was the Chinese-owned supertanker Gem No. 2, hit off Sharjah more than two weeks ago. items.title: Palestinian journalist returns home after 15 months in Israeli detention
items.summary: Palestinian journalist returns home after 15 months in Israeli detention Palestinian journalist Farah Abu Ayyash has returned home to her family following 450 days of detention in Israeli prisons, according to a report by the Islamic Republic News Agency (Irna). Abu Ayyash, a West Bank correspondent for Iran's Tasnim News Agency, was freed on Thursday night after the Ofer Prison military court ordered her release, dismissing the charges brought against her after she served 15 months under administrative detention. According to Irna, Abu Ayyash was initially detained on 6 August 2025, during an overnight military raid on her family home in Beit Ummar, north of Hebron. The outlet reported that her arrest was tied to her journalistic work covering local developments across the southern West Bank for Tasnim. The report further noted that repeated procedural delays prolonged her case, keeping her detained without formal resolution under administrative detention at Damon Prison. Irna also reported that the correspondent was allegedly subjected to torture and mistreatment while in custody.

A total of 277 vessel transits were recorded in the strait during the seven days to October 28, comprising 155 inbound and 122 outbound movements. The combined figure, which includes automatic identification system (AIS) observations and US-reported facilitated transits, was approximately 70 percent below pre-conflict levels. UKMTO said AIS-observed transits increased to 64 from 47 the previous week, while US-reported facilitated movements remained broadly stable. The US Naval Cooperation and Guidance for Shipping (NCAGS) estimates that about 80% of transits through the strait involve energy carriers. items.title: Merz says Germany working to end Iran war that has cost Europe $112bn
items.summary: Merz says Germany working to end Iran war that has cost Europe $112bn German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has said that Germany was working to bring Iran war to an end as soon as possible as the conflict has added more than 100 billion euros ($112bn) to Europe’s energy costs over the past eight months. Speaking to reporters in Seoul on Friday, he said Germany was coordinating and stepping up diplomatic efforts to bring the conflict to an end, while stressing that the "conflict cannot be resolved militarily". “Businesses and consumers in Europe have paid more than 100 billion euros extra because energy has become more expensive as a result of this conflict,” he said. “We therefore also have an economic interest in bringing this conflict to an end as quickly as possible.”

items.title: Iran slams Canada for supporting UAE claim over three Gulf islands
items.summary: Iran slams Canada for supporting UAE claim over three Gulf islands Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei has criticised Canada's support for the United Arab Emirates' claim to three Gulf islands, questioning Ottawa's commitment to territorial integrity and national sovereignty. In a post on X, Baqaei said the UAE, established in 1971, was laying claim to Abu Musa and the Greater Tunb and Lesser Tunb despite "historical records and geographical and documented evidence establishing their Iranian ownership". He said the islands had been part of Iran for millennia, long before the UAE federation was established, and criticised Canada's prime minister for echoing what he called an “absurd claim”. Baqaei invoked Canada's own history of defending its sovereignty, citing the American invasion during the War of 1812, the Montreal Annexation Manifesto of 1849 and US President Donald Trump's repeated remarks about making Canada the 51st US state. “How can it take sides in a fabricated dispute and endorse an unfounded territorial claim that amounts to dangerous adventurism?” he said.

items.title: Oman evacuates crew of tanker set ablaze near Hormuz
items.summary: Oman evacuates crew of tanker set ablaze near Hormuz Oman said on Friday it had rescued 25 sailors from a merchant ship that was targeted and set ablaze, as Iran reported three oil tankers had been halted while crossing the blockaded Strait of Hormuz. Muscat’s navy “carried out an evacuation operation for 25 crew members of the merchant ship Riti, flying the Panamanian flag, after it was targeted, which led to a fire breaking out on board”, Oman’s Maritime Security Centre said in a statement. The crew members were provided with medical care, the Omani statement said. The MarineTraffic ship-tracking website described the Riti as a crude oil tanker. In a video released earlier on Friday, Centcom chief Brad Cooper said US forces had “successfully cleared the strait’s internationally recognised primary transit routes of Iranian sea mines”. Iran’s Revolutionary Guard Corps said separately that three oil tankers had been halted after encountering unspecified “incidents” or hitting mines.

items.title: Centcom chief says Hormuz routes remain clear as Iran reports interceptions
items.summary: Centcom chief says Hormuz routes remain clear as Iran reports interceptions The head of US Central Command (Centcom), Admiral Brad Cooper, has claimed that the main international shipping routes through the Strait of Hormuz are clear of Iranian sea mines and that commercial vessels are sailing freely through the waterway. In a video posted on Cencom's X account, Cooper said he flew over the strait earlier this week and saw dozens of commercial vessels transiting the area. “Here’s what I didn’t see: I didn’t see the IRGC out there at all,” he said, claiming Iran’s navy was “all at the bottom of the sea”. The remarks come as Iran has repeatedly claimed that it maintains control over the strait. Earlier, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it had stopped two tankers attempting to cross the southern part of the waterway, accusing them of using “unauthorised routes” with US military support.
